title: Equivalence of maximal and generic reachability for non-universal Variational Quantum Circuits
abstract: Employing problem-specific non-universal Variational Quantum Circuits aligned with a suitable state preparation has become a standard approach to counter the difficulty in training universal ansätze. However, due to their non-universality, diagnosing their reachability and trainability remains reference-state-specific. In this work, we establish the equivalence of maximal reachability and generic reachability over arbitrary reference states as a consequence of the \emph{principal orbit-type theorem}. Thereafter, assuming that the global minimum of the cost function is achieved on a subset that can be described as the image of a smooth function, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for non-zero probability of reachability under generically sampled reference states. Furthermore, when the solution set is assumed to be realised through a real analytic map that embeds a solution manifold, we show that local surjectivity is generically obtained on the entire solution manifold if it is attained at a single point. As a practical design rule, the need for local surjectivity automatically translates to a necessary dimensional criterion: reachability requires the target set's topological dimension to be at least as large as the co-dimension of the generic orbit. Numerical simulations show that finite-depth optimisation consistently fails when the dimensional obstruction applies, while unobstructed cases show improved convergence.
summary: This theoretical work rigorously analyzes the limitations of Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) by establishing conditions for state reachability on the quantum state manifold. It derives a crucial dimensional criterion stating that the target set must have sufficient topological dimension relative to the circuit's generic orbit. This provides a powerful diagnostic tool for designing trainable and effective quantum algorithms.
main_problem: The paper establishes the mathematical conditions for determining the reachability and trainability of non-universal Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) on the pure state manifold.
main_result: It proves the equivalence of maximal and generic reachability and derives a necessary dimensional criterion: the target set's dimension must be at least as large as the co-dimension of the generic orbit for non-zero probability of reachability.
method: The analysis employs tools from differential geometry, including the principal orbit-type theorem, the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM), and measure theory to analyze the image of the VQC parameter map.
model_or_system: The system involves Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) acting on an n-qubit system, whose dynamics are analyzed on the pure state manifold (MN). The focus is on the orbit generated by the VQC parameters from a reference state.
key_observables: Reachability probability, rank of the QFIM, topological dimension of the solution manifold, and the co-dimension of the generic orbit.
important_parameters: The depth of the VQC (finite-depth optimization), the structure of the reference state ($\psi_r$), and the target state ($\psi^*$).
main_assumptions: Assumes the global minimum of the cost function lies on a smooth subset and that the solution set can be realized via a real analytic map embedding a solution manifold.

paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the equivalence of maximal and generic reachability using the principal orbit-type theorem, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions based on the smoothness of the cost function minimum, and concluding with a dimensional criterion derived from local surjectivity arguments.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical guarantees regarding the limitations of current quantum machine learning approaches, specifically diagnosing when VQCs are fundamentally incapable of reaching a target state due to geometric constraints.
